messages:
marta: thinking out loud 1: should the edge keep JSON while the gateway translates to proto for internal calls? top concerns: dashboardability, accurate quota/billing, and a low-friction canary UX.

sam: my vote: keep edge JSON for ergonomics, do translation at gateway. typed RPCs internally make telemetry + contract checking way easier.

lee: agreed on translation, but we saw ~20-40ms overhead on small requests when we added proto marshalling. it's fine for heavier routes (embeddings) but might matter for metadata endpoints.

ana: can we mitigate by async enrichment? gateway forwards request immediately and sends an enriched copy for routing/telemetry downstream? tough for strict quotas though.

marta: quota/billing needs origin mapping at the time of intake. we can't delay attribution. any ideas?

dmitri: do attribution at edge and carry signed metadata into gateway -> services trust the signed envelope. Edge enforces tenant token checks and quota tokens. Services keep lightweight checks for safety.

rik: technical sketch: edge signs a small header blob `x-rd-auth` (kid+sig) and gateway expands it into proto AnnotatedRequest. Services verify signature if needed. This avoids re-checking auth in every service.

lee: signing is good. also add `x-rd-route-hint` so gateway can precompute caching keys and quota buckets before fanout. saves a round of introspection downstream.

sam: telemetry: we need a compact span attribute set so dashboards don't explode. propose: `rd.client_id`, `rd.tenant`, `rd.route`, `rd.proto_version`, `rd.translation` (values: "none","proto","fallback").

marta: nice. for rollout UX: console toggle + header opt-in? we want experiments where small % of requests are translated even if all clients are JSON.

dmitri: implement percent-based sampling in the gateway: routing key -> deterministic hash -> N% path. Also allow header override `x-rd-proto-preview=1` to opt in for devs.

rik: fallback rules: if translation or proto fail, gateway should fall back to passthrough and tag span `rd.translation=fallback`. Emit a structured event for alerting.

lee: ops checklist for canary that we used in spike:
- enable translation toggle in console (service:gateway)
- set canary percent to 5% in region us-west
- turn on `rd.translation` attribute in tracing and logs
- enable `x-rd-proto-preview` header for manual opt-ins
- add dashboard panels: translation failures, p50/p95 delta, quota-rejects by origin

ana: dashboard panels I want to add:
- cohort compare: translated vs passthrough latency (p50/p95/99)
- translation-failure rate per route
- quota attribution mismatch (edge vs service) alerts
- top failing tenants during canary

sam: small proto example for gateway envelope:

```proto
message GatewayEnvelope {
  string request_id = 1;
  string client_id = 2;
  string route = 3;
  bytes body_json = 4; // opaque during opt-in
}
```

gateway sets headers: `x-rd-route`, `x-rd-request-id`, `x-rd-signature` and sends GatewayEnvelope to internal gRPC. Services can either decode body_json or run new proto flow.

marta: logging format: we should surface `origin=edge|gateway|service`, `translation=none|proto|fallback`, and `quota_origin=edge|service` in all access logs. console can use these to filter rejections.

rik: on backward compatibility: we must support both code paths indefinitely for a while. add a runtime flag to disable proto path per-route so we can quickly disable if we see regressions.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled: gateway/translator v3.1 -> 5% us-west at 2025-09-02T09:10:00Z (manual rollback window 30m) :calendar:

lee: one more note 1: kv-cache keys must be consistent between proto and JSON paths or we'll lose cache efficiency. recommend gateway derives cache-key from route + canonicalized body JSON hash and passes it as `x-rd-cache-key`.

ana: i'll add canonicalization util to telemetry lib and dashboard queries.

dmitri: I'll implement edge token-bucket limiter and emit `x-rd-quota-origin=edge` header when consenting. Services will log when they enforce service-side limits.

sam: I'll own perf benchmark and can run an A/B with 0/5/25% translation.

marta: perfect. i'll write a short RFC summarizing: edge JSON + signed envelope header, gateway-side proto enrichment with translational fallback, edge-first quota attribution + service soft checks, deterministic canary routing + header opt-in, telemetry attributes + dashboard panels. will ping owners for review. thanks all. :raised_hands:
